narrative.headline: ⚠️ THIS RECONSTRUCTION DOES NOT RECONCILE with Polymarket's own profit figure for the wallet, so the numbers below are wrong by an unknown amount — most likely it exits through an activity type the feed does not publish, such as a merge. Read the shape, not the totals. hihhe deployed $2,321,318 across 1,413 events in 68 days and finished $28,357 — a yield of +1.22% on money at risk. 100% of that capital went in after kick-off, the median position was held 31.1 min, and the median ticket was $43.04.

sections.title: What it does
paragraphs: **Archetype: In-play short-horizon trader, Near-certainty grinder, Systematic / automated.**
— *In-play short-horizon trader* (high confidence): 99.5% of capital goes in after kick-off, 0.5% before; median hold 31.1 min, 5% of round trips close inside 10 minutes.
— *Near-certainty grinder* (high confidence): 99% of capital enters above 0.90 — thin margins, high turnover; capital recycled 95.0× against a peak book of $24,442.
— *Systematic / automated* (high confidence): 6,142 fills across 1,413 events, 89 fills per active day; median ticket $43.04 — size is uniform, which is what a script looks like.
It trades 1,539 markets over 1,413 fixtures — 6,142 fills, 89 per active day over 69 days with activity. It buys at an average of 0.987 and sells at 0.994.
Where it plays: ATP Tour (73% of capital, +1%), WTA Tour (27% of capital, +1%).
Market types: moneyline 93%, tennis_first_set_winner 5%, tennis_set_winner 2%.

sections.title: Where the money comes from
paragraphs: **The money is made after settlement time**: $1,379,580 deployed there returned $18,744 (+1.4%), which is 66% of all profit on 59% of the capital.
Return falls with the entry price: +6% in the 0.90–0.95 band against +1% in 0.95–1.01. The profitable end is the expensive end — this is a wallet paid for conviction, not for cheapness.
Exits: 8% sold back into the book, 92% redeemed at settlement, 0% simply left to resolve (-$4.62 of that expired worthless).

sections.title: How it evolved
paragraphs: Across 3 complete months the book grew from $254,845 to $806,215 of monthly turnover, and the yield is **flat** — +1.7% over the first 1 month(s) against +1.2% over the last 2. Yield roughly constant across the life of the wallet.
2026-10 is still in progress ($34,677 deployed, +1.1%) and is excluded from the trend.

Day to day it wins 67 of 68 sessions — best $2,344, worst -$1,156, longest losing streak 1 days. Peak open book $24,442; the cumulative cash floor is -$14,736, so it had to carry a real bankroll, not just recycle winnings.

sections.title: Is the edge real?
paragraphs: Bootstrapped over 1,413 events (resampled by event, not by lot, because lots inside one fixture are the same bet taken repeatedly): yield +1.22%, 95% CI [+1.02%, +1.42%], p(≤0) = 0.0000. The interval clears zero — the edge in this wallet's own record is real.

Concentration: top event 6% of profit, top 5 15%, top 10 21%; 100% of events profitable. Drop the 200 best individual lots and it still makes $9,494 (+0.41%). The result does not depend on a handful of bets.

Reconciliation: Polymarket says $28,309 all-time, counted before fees; on the same basis (P&L plus $643.56 of fees paid) we reconstruct $29,001 — a gap of -$691.28 (2.4%). **That gap is large enough to matter — read the numbers as approximate.**

sections.title: What is not established
paragraphs: ⚠️ Only 0% of this wallet's capital is in competitions we recognise as football (0% is unrecognised). The 110-130' whistle window is a football fact and means nothing on the rest — read the timing table for football wallets only.

⚠️ Selection bias on the wallet itself. You are reading it because someone pointed at it. The statistics describe the edge in its own record; they cannot tell you how many identically-shaped wallets blew up unseen.
⚠️ `lb-api` 'volume' is SHARES, not dollars, and its windowed figures do not reconcile. Only `window=all` is used here.
